name: Wait State
author: Jeremy Longshore
description: Shows when work is stalled on CPU, memory, or I/O using Linux pressure stall information, with live severity, six hours of bounded history, and plain-language diagnostics.

barWidget.description: CPU usage says the machine is busy. Wait State says whether useful work is stuck waiting for CPU, memory, or I/O. The bar shows the worst current bottleneck; the panel carries short and long pressure windows, full-stall visibility, persistent history, and an honest explanation of what each signal can prove.

schema.label: Refresh interval
schema.description: How often to read the three fixed /proc/pressure files. History is sampled at most once every 15 seconds regardless of this setting.

schema.label: Bar resource
schema.description: Worst follows the resource with the highest current avg10 partial-stall percentage.

schema.label: Default history
schema.description: Initial time range for the pressure history chart.

schema.label: Warning threshold
schema.description: Partial-stall avg10 percentage that marks pressure as elevated. This is a display threshold, not a universal kernel limit.

schema.label: Critical threshold
schema.description: Partial-stall avg10 percentage that marks pressure as severe. It is always normalized above the warning threshold.
